When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian score **83** (strong buy) vs Macro regime CONTRACTION at **70%** confidence, with **3** risk-off signals aligned
One gauge says buy fear while the other two say stay defensive. Trust the regime read for sizing, because the contrarian score needs a stress event (backwardation, credit strain) that has not appeared yet.
⚠ These two disagree: Divergence composite zone CALM at **39.5%** of pairs diverging vs Mother jaws score **100**, with two pairs at **100**

Today's tension
Contraction regime and a **83** contrarian buy score collide while the Nasdaq 100 slides **-5.0%** in five days.
Bull
The contrarian gauge reads **83**, which points to capitulation, and the Russell 2000 is holding at **-0.2%** while the Nasdaq 100 absorbs the damage. Volatility stress is low, with the Crash Index at only **2/10** and VIX backwardation inactive.
Bear

AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The tape is split. Price stress is low, with the Crash Index at 2/10 and no VIX backwardation. The macro read is defensive: CONTRACTION at 70% confidence and a regime score of 56 in transition with a risk-off bias.

The tension sits underneath. The contrarian score of 83 wants you to buy fear, but fear has only shown up in one place: the Nasdaq 100 at -5.0% over five days, while the Russell 2000 sits at -0.2%. That is a leadership problem in big growth stocks. It has not become a broad market problem.

For positioning, you keep gross exposure moderate and avoid chasing the contrarian signal until the options market confirms capitulation. Skew is active and the VIX Spike probability reads 50%, so hedges are priced for a move that has not arrived. Add risk in tranches if the Nasdaq weakness stays contained to a few mega-cap names.

The main risk is the Nasdaq slide spreading to small caps, which would show up as the Russell breaking below its -0.2% five-day reading. A flip to backwardation takes the stance fully defensive. A contraction reading that drops from 70% confidence would open the door to the contrarian buy.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence measures how far a pair of assets has moved apart from its usual relationship. Correlation drift is the change in how tightly they move together, for example a pair that moved in lockstep and now moves independently or in opposite directions.

The composite zone is CALM, with 39.5% of 43 pairs diverging and a net bias of -1 (8 bearish, 9 bullish). That reads as a balanced picture. The mother jaws score of 100 says something else, because individual relationships have broken sharply. AUD/JPY drifted from +0.57 to -0.37, so the risk-on currency pair has stopped behaving like a risk gauge. EWJ vs SPY flipped from -0.50 to +0.38.

The SPY and TLT correlation moved from +0.75 to -0.17, so stocks and bonds have stopped moving together. That is a diversification-friendly shift for a balanced portfolio. The staples and discretionary pair (XLP/XLY) at 86 and 85 shows defensive and cyclical sectors decoupling, which fits the rotation out of the Nasdaq. The 10-year minus 2-year yield spread at 80 adds a rates twist to that picture.

Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Leadership is scattered, with no single region driving the global tape. In Asia, Korea's KOSPI leads at +1.9% while Shanghai lags at -1.6%, so the strength is local to Korea. In Europe, France's CAC leads at +2.6% and the FTSE is flat at -0.1%.

The US is the weak link. The Nasdaq 100 trails at -5.0% while the Russell 2000 holds at -0.2%. Money is leaving mega-cap growth and not leaving equities altogether. In crypto, ETH is at +0.6% and SOL at -3.6%, which shows speculative appetite thinning at the edges.

For today's US session, expect Nasdaq heavy names to stay under pressure unless Europe's +2.6% strength carries over. A Russell break lower would be the signal that the rotation has turned into a broader sell-off.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 2/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The Crash Index at 2/10 and the VIX Spike Detector at tier 1/4 (BROAD) agree with each other. Both say stress is low to moderate. Price action is orderly, and the options market has not priced a vol expansion into the near term.

Two details deserve attention. Skew is active, which means downside puts cost more than upside calls, so some investors are buying protection. Backwardation is inactive, so the front of the VIX curve is not yet above the back, and that is where real panic shows up. The spike probability of 50% is a coin flip, which tells you the risk is live and still unconfirmed. You treat the Nasdaq's -5.0% drop as a rotation until backwardation says otherwise.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 2/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

How to read
Each row = an independent signal Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY. The structural (DXY, SKEW, MOVE) signal a regime change over 30-90 days. The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

How to read
Aggregation of all panel signals across the 4 cross-asset buckets. RISK-ON = risk appetite (cyclical, equity, EM). RISK-OFF = flight to defensives (TLT, gold, JPY). STRESS = liquidity tension (HYG, MOVE, STLFSI). TOPPING = end-of-cycle signals (concentration, breadth narrowing, defensives leading). Doctrine: a single signal = noise. 3+ aligned in one bucket = real confirmed regime.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
